meta.name: Constructing a Confidence Interval for a Population Mean (7.2)
meta.subject: AP Statistics
meta.description: One-sample t-intervals for a population mean: identify the procedure, check conditions, find t*, calculate margin of error, and construct the interval.

perField.procedureAnswer: Use this checklist: one sample, quantitative data, and estimating a mean μ. That points to a one-sample t-interval.
perField.conditionsMet: All three must work: random sample, 10% condition when sampling without replacement, and n ≥ 30 or no strong skewness/outliers if n < 30.
perField.conditionsExplain: Mention the random condition, the 10% check, and either n ≥ 30 or the sample-shape check for skewness and outliers.
perField.tStarAnswer: For a confidence interval for a mean, use a t critical value with df = n - 1, not a z critical value.
perField.meAnswer: Margin of error = t* × s / √n. Use the sample standard deviation s and divide by the square root of n.
perField.ciLower: First compute the margin of error, then subtract it from x̄ to get the lower bound.
perField.ciUpper: First compute the margin of error, then add it to x̄ to get the upper bound.
